items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: another day, at this music store, I met Roy Eldridge in there.

ctx.x: Do you remember the first day you came to the City...how you came and who you were with?
We came in on a bus and I went and stayed at that hotel right next to Minton's,

what is the name of that hotel? Anyway, all the musicians stayed there and anyway I went right into the hotel, then Minton's was right downstairs. And that was just right for me. Boy oh boy, I'd come downstairs every night and Lester Young would be blowin' and Harold ("Doc") West and, oh gee whiz, Don Byas and I got a chance to really hear all these wonderful people and see them in this New York setting, you know what I mean, and it was just wonderful. And of course Kenny Clarke and Monk and, let's see, Eddie…

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: he was playin' like Roy Eldrige at the time.

ctx.x: Was Elvin on the scene then...?

No, he was a little baby then. But they were in the band and that's how we went to Cincinatti. That's the first time I ever heard Howard McGhee. He came down from Milwaukee with Leonard Gay's band and...Leonard Gay played nice tenor...but Howard was outstanding. He was playing, I'll never forget, his feature was "Body and Soul" and he was playin' like Roy Eldrige at the time. And last time I was in New York, I was on the radio, and he called in and I took him on back, you know. He says, "you start talkin' about…
your feature was 'Body and Soul*', I says, "I wasn't but 16, but you were grown." I says, "But Maggie I'm just playin' with you."
